committedStage.message: perf: compartilhar cargos no custeio de RDO e horas alocadas

candidate: Uncommitted local continuation in the performance worktree. No deployment, new migration, pool changes or backup work.
changes: Load official confirmed missions once for both allocation metadata and complete legacy-window exclusions, including missions without allocations.
Batch individual cycles, general mission cycles and actual plan state only for the returned allocations. Empty allocations skip all three child reads and the duplicate mission relation.
Share the unchanged official/active/confirmed predicate with the existing exported allocation reader; preserve its selection and return contract.

Preserve cycle IDs/dates/order and individual precedence through the existing allocationPeriods/buildEffectiveAllocationIndex functions. Missing mission/plan rows cannot fabricate windows; read failures reject the complete load.
No new cross-request cache, source concurrency cap, index or financial formula; next request reloads mutable sources.

comparisonDesign.method: Synthetic loopback HTTP through real Express and migrated PostgreSQL, persisted hashed sessions, complete body receipt included. No proxy, TLS, browser, external APIs or production load.
comparisonDesign.environment: PostgreSQL 16, one CPU, 768 MiB; API pool eight, shared concurrency four; distributed RDOs, summary point projection. API host not isolated.
comparisonDesign.order: Sequential control/candidate, then candidate/control. No tests or other benchmark workload from this task during timed cohorts.
comparisonDesign.counts: 832 measured responses per cohort: 800 warm (100 per route/profile), eight first-process, eight warmups, 16 after-write. Eight expected access negatives separately.
comparisonDesign.sourceParity: Separate baseline/candidate processes read identical PostgreSQL rows in five states: initial, role/salary/report writes, official allocations, cycle/cancellation writes, plan deactivation. Eight complete normalized results compared per state.
comparisonDesign.sourceFixture: Role history without profiles, overlapping imports, day/night RDO costs outside point, planned hours, individual and general cycles, open ends and pauses; draft/deleted/scenario/inactive missions and confirmed mission without allocations.
comparisonDesign.httpFixture: No official allocations in the stock HTTP fixture. The four-call reduction applies to that case; the populated case is separately verified by real PostgreSQL parity and query counts, not by these HTTP latency samples.

backendSuite.databaseOptIns: Dedicated PostgreSQL opt-ins disabled; real database suites run separately and serially.

coverage: Four detail projection tests, six HTTP benchmark contracts, one point/group regression, one labor source regression.
Zero plan/cycle queries with empty official allocations and a single official mission catalog read.
Actual legacy/index equality for individual and inherited cycles, pauses, open ends, allocation date overrides.
Exclude deleted allocations/missions, draft missions, scenarios and inactive plans; preserve unallocated confirmed mission exclusions.
Observe cycle writes, mission cancellation and plan deactivation on next read; complete rate/result parity, access and worker freshness.

validation.syntax: Changed application, fixture and test files passed node --check; git diff --check passed.
validation.cleanup: Fixture projects outside the two bootstrap internal projects, reports, collaborators, imports, users, sessions, groups, plans, missions, allocations and both cycle tables all counted zero. The owned disposable PostgreSQL container and volumes were removed after validation.

acceptance.queryReduction: Empty official allocations: point HTTP 36 to 32 calls; direct rates 30 to 26, attendance 25 to 21 and diagnosis 29 to 25. Populated official allocations: one call removed per direct calculation (rates 30 to 29). Warm detail/group remain 51-52 and cards 11 with their normal cache behavior.
acceptance.latency: Descriptive sequential cohorts on an unisolated host do not establish causal or statistical p95 acceptance.

ci.note: 61010fcd was committed locally only in this turn; neither it nor the local continuation has a new remote CI result.

limitations: One fresh-process response per route/profile per cohort cannot estimate cold p95 or close the general cold reduction target. Database pages are warm and process imports excluded.
Active pool samples are observations, not per-query wait durations. Submitted-query peaks include pool waiting.
After-write timing starts after commit and measurement preparation; cards retain normal expiry.
Published useful-content/LCP and HTTP acceptance, 24-hour/seven-day operation, and retention policy remain pending. Backups deferred by user.
